html:
SMTO-CTR-0008 — Your request is too long for SMTO to plan

GUID: 75e5f8f9-da60-4b9e-87fe-f6e510996cdb
Slug: task-contract-ingress-size-limit
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • Your message is longer than 64,000 characters, which is more than SMTO can turn into a task plan. SMTO didn't act on it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Move long pasted text, such as logs or documents, into a file and attach it with Add context instead of pasting it into the message. Attached files don't count toward the message length limit.
  2. Keep the message itself to your instructions: what you want done and what the result should look like. A shorter message fits the limit while still saying everything you need.
  3. If it's still too long, split the work into several requests and send each one as its own message. Each request is measured against the limit on its own.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Task contract generated and starts working.

If it still fails

  • If your message is well under 64,000 characters and you still see this, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend the same long message; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Task Contract compiler rejected the source request because its text exceeds the 64,000-character input limit.

What this means

  • compiler_input rejects a source user-request string longer than 64,000 characters before constructing the compiler request. This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.

Why this can happen

  • compiler_input rejects a source user-request string longer than 64,000 characters before constructing the compiler request.

How to diagnose it

  • Measure the actual source text; this guard is not an attachment byte or model output-token limit.

How to fix it

  • compiler_input in src/agent_runtime/native/task_contract.py rejects a source request longer than 64,000 characters before building the compiler request. Shorten the request text or split it into separate tasks while keeping its requirements, and move bulk material into Context attachments, which are referenced by metadata and do not count toward this limit.
  • Reduce or deliberately split the source request while preserving its requirements; use supported context references where appropriate.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The complete intended source fits the supported input boundary through deliberate scoping.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
